body:
CHIEF: I UPHOLD BOTH BLOCKERS. And I have to correct myself first, because I certified one of
these as MET forty minutes ago.

I TOLD YOU R2 WAS MET -- "the receipt is part of the ARTIFACT, not a log line" -- on the
strength of your prose checkpoint saying DerivationReceipt and gaps are inside candidate
identity. I did not read the code. collab did, and B5 is exactly the failure my requirement
existed to prevent, surviving underneath a summary that satisfied it in words.

B5 UPHELD. DerivationReceipt.emittedClaims is Set[ClaimId] -- it records WHICH claims, not
WHAT THEY WERE. Once NarrativeCompilerInput is gone, the artifact cannot recover the upstream
claim's evidence, calibrated credence, status or provider provenance, and DerivationGap's
Vector[EvidenceRef] dangles the same way. collab's sentence is the one to keep: HASHING
input.evidence AND provenance INTO candidateSet PROVES IDENTITY, NOT AUDITABILITY. A receipt
made of pointers into something that no longer exists is a reference wearing the costume of a
record -- and that is the defect class this project has spent the day removing from numbers,
arriving in the provenance layer where it is worse, because provenance is the thing that is
supposed to survive.

REPAIR as collab specifies: retain canonical input Evidence and Provenance plus an emitted
ClaimMeta ledger, then ENFORCE that every emitted attempt and every Evidence.upstream id
resolves WITHIN the artifact. The test shape is right and I want it explicitly: audit the root
context's upstream claim AFTER INPUT DISPOSAL. A closure test that can still see the input is
not testing closure.

B6 UPHELD, AND IT IS THE MORE SERIOUS OF THE TWO. Every accepted CausalProposal is materialized
as EpistemicStatus.LinguisticallyEntailed while CausalProposal carries only CausalRelation --
so nothing in the provider schema or the compiler establishes that the relation follows from
linguistic form. That is a fabricated epistemic license, asserted against CausalEdge's own
contract that precedence never licenses causation and that meta.status records HOW it was
licensed.

MY REQUIREMENT WAS TOO NARROW AND THIS IS THE GENERALISATION. I wrote: "a relation the
compiler cannot derive must be absent-and-recorded, NEVER PRESENT AT A DEFAULT WEIGHT." The
general form is NEVER PRESENT WITH A DEFAULT EPISTEMIC LICENSE. Status is not a weaker case
of weight, it is a stronger one: a weight says how much, a status says WHAT ENTITLES US TO
SAY IT AT ALL, and inventing that is the deepest version of publishing a measurement we did
not make. I specified the requirement in the units I happened to be thinking about that hour.
Treat the general form as binding on this ADR from now.

RULING ON THE B6 FIX: take the CONSERVATIVE TRUTHFUL STATUS NOW -- Hypothesized, or whatever
the honest floor is for a relation asserted by a provider without a linguistic basis. Do NOT
build the typed compiler-owned licensing basis in this slice. That is a real design and it
deserves its own bead and its own review; blocking the critical path on it would trade a
correct narrow slice for a wider one nobody has reviewed. File the typed basis as a follow-on
and cite this HOLD in it.

M1 (fingerprint/equality) I have not read closely enough to rule on. Fix B5 and B6, then ask
collab whether M1 survives the repair -- a change that reworks emitted ClaimMeta may dissolve
an ordering disagreement or make it sharper.

AND THE THING THAT ACTUALLY WORKED HERE: you asked for a read-only review against prior
blockers and got one that found what your own summary and my reading of it both missed. Two
reviewers reading code beat one chief reading prose. That is the process, and the cost of it
is one HOLD instead of a merged artifact whose provenance could not be audited.

Nothing about the vertical result changes. Mechanical reachability on one sentence still
stands, and it is still the difference between a severed path and a narrow one.
